keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: List of 1–5 search terms to analyze on Google Trends. Use this when the user provides specific keywords, topics, or brand names to compare (e.g. ['ChatGPT', 'Gemini', 'Copilot']). Required when requesting interest_over_time / interest_by_region / related_queries / related_topics. Not required when only fetching trending_searches. Maximum 5 keywords — Google enforces this limit on comparison.

geo.title: Geographic Region
geo.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to filter trends by location (e.g. 'US', 'GB', 'IN', 'DE'). Use '' (empty string) for worldwide. This also picks the residential proxy country, which is critical for reliability — Google blocks mismatched IP/geo pairs.

timeframe.title: Timeframe
timeframe.description: Date range for trend data. Past month / 3 months / 12 months are the most reliable; 'all' (since 2004) is the slowest. Overridden by customTimeRange if provided.

property.title: Property / Search Type
property.description: Which Google property to analyze. 'web' is normal Google Search (default and most reliable). Other properties return narrower data — for instance YouTube returns YouTube-specific interest curves, which differ from web search.

category.title: Category ID
category.description: Google Trends category to filter results. Use 0 for all categories (default). Full list at trends.google.com/trends/api/explore (categories list).

dataTypes.title: Data Types to Extract
dataTypes.description: Which Google Trends data types to fetch in one run. interest_over_time = temporal curve (0–100 relative). interest_by_region = geographic breakdown. related_queries = top/rising search terms. related_topics = top/rising Knowledge Graph topics. trending_searches = daily top searches by country (does not need keywords). Pick as many as you need — they share one session, so adding more is cheap.

trendingSearchesGeo.title: Trending Searches Country
trendingSearchesGeo.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for daily trending searches (only used when 'trending_searches' is in dataTypes). Example: 'US', 'GB', 'IN'. Defaults to the value of geo. Trending searches are not available for every country — US/GB/IN/JP/DE are the most reliable.

maxResults.title: Max Results
maxResults.description: Maximum total number of records to return across all dataTypes. The actor stops + charges once this limit is hit. Default 500 covers typical use; raise it for full multi-keyword exports.

customTimeRange.title: Custom Date Range
customTimeRange.description: Override 'timeframe' with a specific date range. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g. '2023-01-01 2024-01-01'). Leave empty to use the timeframe enum. NOT a single date — must be two dates separated by a space.

outputFormat.title: Output Format
outputFormat.description: How to structure output. 'flat' = one record per data point (default — best for CSV exports and AI/LLM pipelines). 'summary' = same flat structure today (reserved for future grouped output).
enumTitles: Flat — one record per data point (default, best for AI/CSV)
Summary — one record per keyword with nested arrays
